data.title: Selce – Hrádok, a small summit hillfort on limestone
data.excerpt: Hrádok above the Selčiansky potok is small in size but important: a ridge anticline of limestone at 780 m a.s.l., with rock faces 2–7 m high and a now barely visible rampart closing off two small summit platforms from the south-east. A hoard of silver Roman denarii, finds of the Lusatian and Púchov cultures, iron arrowheads of the Migration Period and post-Great Moravian sherds show how long the site remained in use.
data.metaTitle: Selce – Hrádok, a small hillfort on a limestone crag
data.metaDescription: Hrádok near Selce is a small summit hillfort on a limestone anticline at 780 m, with Lusatian, Púchov and Slavic finds and a hoard of Roman denarii.

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: The hillfort lies on the right bank of the Selčiansky potok in the cadastral area of the village, at an elevation of 780 m.

keyFacts.label: Geological setting
keyFacts.value: The hillfort is a ridge anticline formed of limestone rock whose faces are 2–7 m high, covered with a thin layer of loamy soil.

keyFacts.label: Fortification
keyFacts.value: From the south-east the two small platforms on the summit were protected by a rampart, which today is only very indistinct.

keyFacts.label: Puzzling pits
keyFacts.value: Within the hillfort there are two pits several metres deep and wide whose purpose is unclear; they may, for instance, have been cisterns for water, of modern or of earlier date.

keyFacts.label: Hoard of Roman coins
keyFacts.value: In the 1930s a hoard of silver Roman denarii of several emperors (chiefly Marcus Aurelius) and two silver brooches was found; in 1999 a further 6 denarii from the period 117–195 AD were added, published by Dr Kolníková in 2001.

keyFacts.label: Occupation in several periods
keyFacts.value: The excavation by Dr Karol Pieta (AVANS 1988) attested occupation by the Lusatian culture (the Final Bronze Age), the Púchov culture (the Late La Tène period), the Migration Period and the Middle Ages.

keyFacts.label: Slavic finds
keyFacts.value: In the 1950s V. Budinský-Krička found Slavic sherds dated to the post-Great Moravian period; further Slavic sherds from the survey by P. Mosný were dated by Dr Mácelová to the 10th–11th century.

keyFacts.label: Presumed function
keyFacts.value: The function of the hillfort in the Slavic period is unclear; it may have served as a refuge, a watch post or the seat of a nobleman.

children.text: On the right bank of the Selčiansky potok, in the cadastral area of the village at an elevation of 780 m, lies a summit hillfort called Hrádok, small in size but important. It is a ridge anticline formed of limestone rock whose faces are 2–7 m high. The limestone crag is covered with a thin layer of loamy soil. From the south-east two small platforms on the summit were protected by a rampart, which at present is only very indistinct. Within the hillfort there are two pits several metres deep and wide whose purpose is still unclear to me; nor do I know whether they were created only in modern times, or whether the original inhabitants dug them, for example, as cisterns for water.

In the 1930s a hoard of silver Roman coins (denarii) and two silver brooches was found here. They are denarii of several Roman emperors, the largest number of them belonging to denarii of Marcus Aurelius, who, as we know, took part in one of the campaigns of the Roman army directly on the territory of present-day Slovakia. There are also coins of Trajan and Didius Julianus. In 1999 six Roman denarii were found on the slope of Hrádok, published by Dr Kolníková in 2001. They are coins of the emperors Septimius Severus and Trajan, that is, of the period between 117 and 195 AD, from which Dr Kolníková concludes that this need not be a single hoard concealed at one time, but that the coins may have been hidden at different times.

During the excavation by Dr Karol Pieta (AVANS 1988) an assemblage of pottery and metal objects of the Lusatian culture of the Final Bronze Age was recovered at the hillfort, as well as finds of the Púchov culture of the Late La Tène period (an iron brooch), of the Migration Period (iron three-edged arrowheads) and medieval finds.

In the 1950s a survey was carried out by V. Budinský-Krička. He found Slavic sherds here decorated with broader horizontal lines, which he dated to the post-Great Moravian period. Among the Púchov material from the survey by P. Mosný three diagnostic Slavic sherds from the base of the body of a vessel were found, which Dr Mácelová dates broadly to the 10th–11th century. Its function in the Slavic period is unclear; it may be assumed that it served as a refuge, or as a watch post, or as the seat of a nobleman.

children.text: The hillfort is not marked in any way and because of its position it is also somewhat difficult to find, since no waymarked path leads to it. In spite of that, the hillfort has been plundered by metal detectorists. It is also very densely overgrown with scrub and trees. I recommend a visit.
